findings.summary: The facsimile image alt text exposes the internal zero-based/raw page index instead of the reader page label.
findings.consequence: Screen-reader users hear labels such as `Sida 1` for an editor page whose visible bibliographic page label is `-2`, and the alt text omits the title/author context used by the main reader facsimile component.
findings.evidence: The owned template binds `:alt="`Sida ${page.pageIndex}`"` on the facsimile image. `EditorReaderPage` also carries `pageName`, `title`, and contributors, and the SSR editor test verifies the same fixture has `.reader-context-ssr .pages` text `-2 av -1` while `pageIndex` is 1. The established `ReaderFacsimileImage` alt includes title, author, and `page.pageName`.
findings.recommendation: Build the image alt from the bibliographic label, for example `Sida ${page.pageName ?? page.pageIndex}` plus available title/contributor context, rather than only the raw editor index.
verification: Checked shared/types/editor-reader.ts for available pageName/title/contributor fields.
Compared app/components/reader/ReaderFacsimileImage.vue alt handling and test/ssr/editor-reader.spec.ts expectations for the same fixture.

findings.summary: The editor facsimile image has no client-side error state or alert when the image request fails.
findings.consequence: If the selected facsimile image GET fails after the editor page data has loaded, the reader surface can degrade to a broken image without an accessible failure message or recovery state. This is especially exposed when users switch to a different facsimile size client-side.
findings.evidence: The owned template renders the `` with `@load="updateImageWidth"` but no `@error` branch. The established `ReaderFacsimileImage` dependency keeps `imageFailed`, hides the failed image, and renders a `role="alert"` message for the same class of facsimile asset failure.
findings.recommendation: Add the same local failure state used by `ReaderFacsimileImage`, or factor the editor facsimile rendering through a shared component that emits load width while preserving the existing error alert behavior.
